segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: When you realized that the object was not an overturned car, what did you then think it was?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: I don't know. I didn't think nothing. I just ran, I didn't... I didn't... I was so scared, I didn't think.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: What was it that scared about it?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: The noise. The appareance of the object.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: What are your current thoughts about what happened back then, 35 years ago?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: I don't know. I don't think about it very much. I don't go there. I don't talk about that no more. But people are still calling me up about it.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Did this incident have a big affect on your life?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: It didn't affect my life at all. It's just something that happened and I just wen on from there.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Hiw king were you with the police department?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: Fifteen years total. But just for two years after the incident and then I quit. I got transferred to landfill, you know, filling in land. I'm still doing it today."

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Has the town of Socorro changed since the incident?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: No, not at all. It's still a little town, nothing much.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: What do you think it was that you saw that day in 1964?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: I still don't know. It was nothing from here though. It's something from some other place, I guess. I don't think it was a secret project or nothing like that."

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: But the two figures you saw standing by the object, they looked pretty normal didn't they?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: I didn't see no figures. I just thought I did from way back up the road there. I didn't actually saw them. I thought I saw some coveralls there, but actually I didn't see them n1Two hours after the incident, when Zamora was first questioned about his sighting by FBI agent Byrnes, Zamora was told that it would be better if he didn't mention seeing the two small figures in white, because no one would believe him. More than three decades later, Zamora still had a hard time admitting to strangers that he had indeed seen these figures. Or had he?.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Did you ever figure out what those markins were on the object?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: No, I haven't figured it out. Nobody has, I guess.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: One person has recently tried to explain your sighting by saying that there was a hot-air balloon race at the tome, and that what you saw was one of the balloons making a brief stop. What do you think of this idea?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: People have said all sort of things. At that time, everybody knew what it was. Everybody had an explanation. They said it was a 'pogo' n2a vertical takeoff and landing aircraft, it was a hot air balloon, that it was a vortex, you know, one of those funnels that come down. They've said a lot of things, but I know what I saw. And it wasn't any of those things.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Have you seen anything else like it since?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: No.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: Do you believe in extraterrestrial life?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: I don't know. Maybe. I saw something, but I don't know what it was.

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: What does your wife think about all this?

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: She thinks I'm crazy. [Laughs]

segments.speaker: interviewer
segments.text: All wives say that about their husbands, though.

segments.speaker: interviewee
segments.text: That's true. [Laughs]
